A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Eagle study and are readable throughout. The comparison includes all figures, tables and references, plus v2's Appendix A; v1 has no separate appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original encoder, fusion, pre-alignment and encoder-selection experiments, benchmark results and qualitative model outputs.

after.justification: V2 reports original experiments throughout Sections 2–3 and Appendix A, including additional training-recipe controls and revised benchmark results.

M1.justification: Section 2.5 and Figure 3 change joint pretraining from updating only the projector with frozen encoders to updating both projector and vision encoders. This modifies one stage of the existing pipeline; the encoder architecture, channel concatenation, individual pre-alignment and greedy encoder selection remain.

E1.justification: Overall dataset and task coverage is retained. Eagle1.8M's sources already appear in v1's advanced training mixture, and benchmarks newly used throughout v2's ablations already appear elsewhere in v1. Their reassignment broadens individual experiments without introducing new overall domains or test scenarios.

E2.justification: V2 drops the separately listed CLIP-only and ConvNeXt-only controls from the fusion comparison in Table 4, and Eagle-X4 variants from the main comparison corresponding to v1 Table 8. The external MLLM baselines and five fusion strategies remain; newly cited Prismatic is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The reported design-space training setup changes from 934k SFT samples to Eagle1.8M, and its six/seven-benchmark comparisons are replaced by an eleven-benchmark evaluation battery. V2 also introduces additional training-budget and staged-data controls. High-resolution efficiency reporting changes from whole-pipeline tokens/second to encoder images/second at batch size four, alongside parameter counts and FLOPs.

E4.justification: New Tables 7 and 13 test extra SFT epochs, encoder unfreezing during pretraining, and alternative data mixtures across training stages. Table 5 adds frozen-encoder configurations with pre-alignment, completing previously missing controls. Figure 4 adds computational-cost comparisons across encoder combinations. These substantially extend the original ablations, although two qualitative expert-comparison examples are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates. Benchmark averages and the new encoder-selection curve do not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Numerous ablation and final-model results are replaced, with additional training and efficiency results. For CLIP+ConvNeXt, Table 4 changes channel-concatenation/sequence-append averages from 658.2/657.2 to 681.5/690.5, reversing their ranking under the revised setup. Llama3-8B Eagle's MMVP entry changes from 71.6 to 52.0 in v1 Table 9 versus v2 Table 8. These revisions should not be interpreted as controlled same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or mathematical derivations. V2's explanation of normalized benchmark averaging documents evaluation rather than introducing new theoretical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's main contributions and conclusion retain the same claims: systematic encoder-design exploration, competitive simple concatenation, benefits from encoder unfreezing and pre-alignment, and strong Eagle benchmark performance.

C2.justification: Section 2.2 now acknowledges degradation when unfreezing CLIP at its original resolution and presents 448-resolution interpolation as an efficiency tradeoff behind 672-resolution accuracy. V1 instead reported no native-resolution degradation and favored 448 on accuracy. V2 also removes the conjecture that CLIP-dominated representations explain injection-based fusion's weaker results.

D1.justification: V2 explicitly supplies the encoder learning rate, Cambrian pretraining/SFT batch size of 1024, and encoder-throughput batch size. It removes v1's explicit Cambrian sample counts, InternVL pixel-shuffle-removal footnote and CLIP checkpoint link. The project URL and other encoder checkpoint links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Prismatic VLM and explicitly distinguishes Eagle's encoder-focused ablations from its broader design-space exploration. It also replaces the ConvNeXt V2 reference with A ConvNet for the 2020s. Most related-work coverage and the overall research positioning remain.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. V2 edits grammar and setup explanations, names the training mixture Eagle1.8M, adds acknowledgments and appendix sections, and updates author, affiliation and conference text. These are limited narrative revisions rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the exploration diagram, revises the overview charts, and replaces the encoder-selection table with a table-and-curve figure. Main ablation tables become compact summaries with detailed appendix tables. Qualitative examples are recomposed, while v1 Figures 5–6 largely reappear as appendix Figures 7 and 6. These substantially change the visual organization.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful training-budget/data controls and computational-cost evidence absent from v1. However, its summaries conflict with their appendix details: unfrozen ConvNeXt averages 682.1 in Table 3 versus 659.7 in Table 10, and SAM/DINOv2 score assignments differ between Figure 4 and Table 12. These unexplained inconsistencies affect central design evidence. The stronger experimental coverage and weaker reporting consistency prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
